guidelines.detail: general guideline covering EXS-013 (example 27) and this example

same as LRN-079 (The description states that a senior participant checks the recommendation and may mark the claim with a status. The reference models the check and marking as activities, while the generated model omits the check and uses a gateway in place of the marking activity. This matches learned guideline LRN-079. I also checked the extra end event X2; it is not relevant to this guideline.)

refines FID-02 (The description distinguishes examination, checking, and marking actions, while the records show those reference activities have no counterparts in the generated model. This refines FID-02 by making explicit that each distinct action must remain identifiable as its own activity. I have not relied on M4: the generated end event may represent the described continuation, so that difference does not e)

same as LRN-079 (The description separates checking the recommendation from marking its outcome. The reference flow includes the marking activity before the branch, while the generated flow proceeds directly from the check to a gateway, using the gateway to represent the status assignment.)

refines FID-01 (The description explicitly states both checking and marking, while the records show both activities missing. This makes FID-01’s instruction to model every stated activity more specific for descriptions where decision work precedes a gateway.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description identifies alternative outcomes or case types that require different follow-up paths, with one path possibly returning to earlier work: Model an exclusive gateway with a separate flow to each applicable follow-up path, including a return flow when a path resumes earlier work.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description identifies alternative outcomes or case types that require different follow-up paths, with one path possibly returning to earlier work
rules_sent_back.source: learned guideline (refines ACT-07), generalized from EXS-013

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a participant checks an item and explicitly assigns or records its status before the process branches: Model the check and status assignment as distinct activities before a gateway; use the gateway to route the flow according to the assigned status.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a participant checks an item and explicitly assigns or records its status before the process branches

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states distinct actions performed in sequence by one or more participants: Model each stated action as a separate activity, using a label that preserves that action and its object; do not use a neighboring activity or a decision gateway to stand in for it.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states distinct actions performed in sequence by one or more participants

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a person checks an item and then marks it or assigns it a status: Model the checking and marking as separate activities, followed by a gateway that routes the process according to the stated status; do not use the gateway in place of either activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a person checks an item and then marks it or assigns it a status
